purpose: Controlled vocabulary for the unit field `system`. 47 free-text values accumulated across 116 units across ~14 species; without a vocabulary a new unit can be tagged with any string and the taxonomy silently fragments. This file is the single source of truth: `system` is a two-level value (domain > system) where domain is one of the 12 top-level families, and system is the anatomical/functional subvalue. Both levels are enforced by GATE 14.
method: Every existing value is preserved as-is (no renaming). Domains are grouped by mechanism: peripheral transduction, central relay, motor command, reflex/CPG, associative learning, memory/cognition, navigation, neuromodulation, homeostasis/state, vocalization/social, motor output, other. GATE 14 fails closed if any unit.system is not in this file.
caveat: Domain is a human-authored classification, not derived from any algorithm. Moving a system between domains requires a version bump and a CHANGELOG entry. Coverage is reported per-domain so gaps are visible.

domains.definition: Peripheral sensory transduction: stimulus-to-neural conversion at or near the sense organ.

systems.note: Generic sense-organ / receptor pool (retinal, glomerular, electrosensory, etc.)

domains.definition: Central relay or gating stage between periphery and higher association cortex/ganglia.

systems.note: Brainstem sensory relay (e.g. red nucleus coordination)

domains.definition: Explicit motor command that drives an effector pool; can be feedforward or goal-directed.

systems.note: Vertebrate spinal motor pool / reflex arc

domains.definition: Stereotyped rhythmic or reflexive circuits: central pattern generators, escape-startle, withdrawal, feeding CPGs.
Reward/punishment-driven conditioning, sensory-to-valence association, odor/food learning.

systems.note: Insect LH innate odor response + learning modulation

domains.definition: Higher-order memory, spatial map, decision, prediction, metacognition. Includes cerebellar timing because climbing-fibre teaching is a memory-forming operation.
Spatial orientation, path integration, heading estimation, spatial mapping.
Diffusible monoamine / amine neuromodulator broadcasts: dopamine, octopamine, serotonergic, noradrenergic.
Whole-body state setting: arousal, sleep/wake flip-flop, circadian, thermal, and glial scaffolding.
Species-specific vocalization and social signaling circuits.
Non-locomotor effector output: pigmentary control, prey-capture aim, vestibulo-ocular stabilisation.
